Two gaps stacked: (a) repair assigns model only after runGeneration RETURNS (repair.ts:576), so a round that throws discards the name resolveModel already produced inside it; (b) model never reaches telemetry at ALL — it is only in the returned payload (repair.ts:717). method: learned from the run: applied = min(config.timeoutMs, remaining), and a row with 900 s of budget applied 20000, so config.timeoutMs = 20000. Source located afterwards at ~/.claude.json:1586, the MCP server's own env block
note: THE SETUP SHELL HAD 60000 EXPORTED AND IT NEVER REACHED THE SERVER. The MCP server's environment comes from its definition in ~/.claude.json, not from the shell that launched Claude Code, so a shell export cannot set it. The analyzer refused to score against the shell value and learned the ceiling from the run instead; without that refusal this run would have produced a confident FAILED verdict against a fix that is correct. Also present there: LOCAL_CODER_MODELS_CSV, pointing at .local-coder/models.csv, which DOES NOT EXIST on that machine — so loadModelCatalog fell back to the built-in catalog (models-csv.ts:16) with a warning nobody was reading. CHECKED, NOT INFERRED: the first version of this note claimed the opposite from the variable's presence alone, which is the same mistake as reading a ceiling off the shell. The correction makes the run MORE reproducible, since the catalog in force is pinned by this repo rather than by a file outside it, and it confirms the selected model independently: qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct-dwq-v2 is the served id of the built-in catalog's first entry

method: the same two files estimate 8882 tokens on the Windows checkout (31,086 B, tests/selection.test.ts carrying 333 CRLF endings) and 8787 on the Mac (30,753 B, LF). Predicted 8882, server reported 8787; the 95-token gap is exactly the 333 carriage returns
note: NOT A BUG — the estimator is byte-exact on both and the INPUT differs. But it is a real term in B14: a byte-based estimate is line-ending dependent, so a request sitting on the boundary can be refused on a CRLF checkout and allowed on an LF one. The 0.9 headroom (~10%) swamps ~1%, so nothing is changed for it. It also means the coverage figures recorded under B0 were counted on CRLF and are therefore the pessimistic side
